# Book of Giants Fragment 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Book of Giants Fragment 1 (The Watchers and Their Offspring) where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 1:7 — "Elioud"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the Nephilim [...] and-the-Elioud [...] who-consumed" — preserves hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "the Nephilim [...] and the Elioud [...] who consumed" — standard formal English |
| PNEUMA | "the Nephilim [...] and the Elioud [...] who devoured everything" — adds "everything" for emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. PNEUMA's addition of "everything" is interpretive. EMET's hyphenation unnecessary for a proper noun passage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:9 — "earth cried out"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-earth cried-out" — hyphenated literalism |
| LOGOS | "the earth cried out" — standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "The very earth screamed out" — intensified with "very" and "screamed" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. PNEUMA's "screamed" is too dramatic for the Aramaic. EMET's hyphenation is excessive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:11 — "devoured mankind"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "and-devoured mankind" — literal |
| LOGOS | "and devoured mankind" — formal |
| PNEUMA | "and ate human beings" — dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET "devoured mankind." The Aramaic carries a sense of ravenous consumption that "ate" fails to convey.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:15 — "brought accusation"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-earth brought accusation against the-lawless-ones" — hyphenated |
| LOGOS | "the earth brought accusation against the lawless ones" — formal |
| PNEUMA | "the earth itself testified against these criminals" — dynamic; changes legal metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Brought accusation" preserves the Aramaic legal idiom better than PNEUMA's "testified."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:19-20 — "imagination/inclination of thoughts"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "every-imagination of-the-thoughts" — echoes Gen 6:5 literally |
| LOGOS | "every inclination of the thoughts" — formal standard |
| PNEUMA | "Every thought in every human mind" — fully restructured |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "every inclination of the thoughts." Preserves the Gen 6:5 echo while remaining readable.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements for Fragment 1: 5*
